newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank to keep cautious monetary policy.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank to keep cautious monetary policy.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand will continue to adopt a cautious monetary policy to solve the inflation and current account deficit problem, a senior BOT official said on Wednesday.

"The central bank will still implement the monetary policy in a cautious way to make sure that the inflation and current account deficit are being solved," the deputy governor Chaiyawat Wibulsawat told reporters.
"We will implement any measures that will generate and sustain the long-term economic stability," he said.
The BOT will not implement any tighter policies on local interest rates which are among the highest in the region.
Chaiyawat said the country's economy had shown signs of improving as can be seen by easing inflationary pressure and a declining current account deficit.
The year-on-year consumer price index rose 4.3 percent in February compared to a 7.4 percent rise the same period a year ago.
The Bank of Thailand has projected the 1997 current account deficit should narrow to less than 7.5 percent of gross domestic product compared to 8.0 percent in 1996.
